summary: A nested loop is a loop inside another loop. Use it for rows and columns: tables, patterns, and grids.
notes: The inner loop starts over at col = 1 each time the outer loop moves to its next row.
console.log() always ends the line, so the times table builds each row in line first. process.stdout.write() prints without ending the line.
col < row in the inner loop makes row 1 print 1 star, row 2 print 2 stars, and so on.
pitfall: Calling console.log(row * col) inside the inner loop puts every number on its own line, because console.log() always ends the line.
contrast: Same structure as Java, with braces showing the nesting. console.log() always ends the line, so you build a row as a string or use process.stdout.write(), where Python uses print(end="") and Java uses print().
